sq.q: A tightly stretched string with fixed end points \(x=0\) and \(x=l\) is initially in a position given by \(y(x,0)=y_0 sin^3 {\pi x \over l}\) . If it is released from rest from this position find the displacement \(y\) at any distance \(x\) from one end at any time \(t\) . Hint: The boundary conditions are: \((i) y(0,t)=0, \forall t>0 \\ (ii) y(l,t)=0, \forall t>0 \\ (iii) {\partial y(x,0) \over \partial t }=0, \forall x \\ (iv) y(x,0)=y_0 sin ^3 {\pi x \over l}.\)

An elastic string is stretched between two points at a distance \(\pi \) apart. In its equilibrium position the string is in the shape of the curve \(f(x)=k(sin x - sin^3 x)\) . Obtain \(y(x,t)\) the vertical displacement if \(y\) satisfies the equation \({\partial^2y \over \partial t^2}={\partial^2 y \over \partial x^2}\)

lq.q: \(\text{A string of length $l$ is fixed at both ends. It is given an initial velocity $\frac{\partial y}{\partial t}(x,0) = v_0 \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi x}{l}\right)$}\\ \text{and initial displacement zero. Find $y(x,t).$ Also solve if the initial velocity is $v_0 \sin^3\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right).$}\)
answer: Step Marks \(\text{Case 1: \(y(x,0)=0\), \(y_t(x,0)= v_0 \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi x}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark) \(\text{General solution: \(y(x,t)= \sum \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right)\left[C_n \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right)+D_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right)\right].\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{\(y(x,0)=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(C_n=0.\) So \(y(x,t)= \sum D_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark) \(\text{\(y_t(x,0)= \sum D_n \left(\dfrac{n\pi c}{l}\right) \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) = v_0 \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi x}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark) \(\text{Thus \(D_2 \left(\dfrac{2\pi c}{l}\right) = v_0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(D_2 = \dfrac{v_0 l}{2\pi c}.\) Other \(D_n=0.\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{So \(y(x,t)= \dfrac{v_0 l}{2\pi c} \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi x}{l}\right) \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi c t}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark) \(\text{Case 2: \(y_t(x,0)= v_0 \sin^3\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right) = \dfrac{v_0}{4}\left[3 \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right) - \sin\left(\dfrac{3\pi x}{l}\right)\right].\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{Similarly, \(y(x,t)= \sum D_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark) \(\text{Then \(y_t(x,0)= \sum D_n \left(\dfrac{n\pi c}{l}\right) \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) = \dfrac{v_0}{4}\left[3 \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right) - \sin\left(\dfrac{3\pi x}{l}\right)\right].\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{Equate: For \(n=1\): \(D_1 \left(\dfrac{\pi c}{l}\right)= \dfrac{3v_0}{4}\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(D_1 = \dfrac{3v_0 l}{4\pi c}.\) For \(n=3\): \(D_3 \left(\dfrac{3\pi c}{l}\right) = -\dfrac{v_0}{4}\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(D_3 = -\dfrac{v_0 l}{12\pi c}.\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{Thus \(y(x,t)= \dfrac{3v_0 l}{4\pi c} \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right) \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi c t}{l}\right) - \dfrac{v_0 l}{12\pi c} \sin\left(\dfrac{3\pi x}{l}\right) \sin\left(\dfrac{3\pi c t}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark)
